_meta.note: Close the parity/cross-runtime coverage gaps the audit found. The HIGH one is a real bug: the Python tick has no review_stuck escalation (node tick.sh emits it past STUCK_TICKS; tick.py wakes review_pending forever), so a stalled adversarial review is a silent infinite stall in Python — a liveness violation — and it hid because the tick's DECISION is never cross-checked (parity compares projector/lint/audit/resolve/report/diagnose-first-line/protocol-KEYS, never the two ticks' data.reason). Each phase adds a cross-runtime proof for a shared surface that was only tested per-runtime; spec-first, the tick proof goes red on the unfixed tick.py. Intentional single-runtime surfaces (exec loop, MCP, bench) are out of scope and stay documented in parity-notes.

tasks.title: Author the tick-parity proof (spec-first, red on the bug)
tasks.description: Spec-first: write docs/howto/gate-examples/tick-parity.sh — for a set of controlled fixtures (each a fresh .hb: a next_task state, a gate_pending state, an all_done state, and crucially a REVIEW-STALL state — a review-owed gate with >= STUCK_TICKS review_wake events and no later verdict), run BOTH runtimes' Stage-A tick on separate fresh copies (node bash .hb/tick.sh; python hb tick --dir) with STUCK_TICKS=3, and assert the two data.reason values are IDENTICAL per fixture. The review-stall fixture is the discriminator: node emits review_stuck, so python must too. Prints TICK-PARITY-OK only when every fixture agrees. On the CURRENT (unfixed) tick.py it MUST go red (node review_stuck vs python review_pending).

tasks.title: Mirror the review_stuck escalation into tick.py
tasks.description: Fix py/src/heartbeat/tick.py review_pending branch to mirror plugin/templates/tick.sh: count review_wake events for the review-owed gate since its last review_passed/review_failed/gate_passed (a helper like _review_wakes_since_verdict); if that count >= STUCK_TICKS, emit a review_stalled event once (guarded by a .review-stuck-alerted flag, matching the .noprogress-alerted / .deadlock-alerted pattern) and wake review_stuck (with gate + no_review + the run-the-refuter hint), else _sleep review_waiting; otherwise clear the flag, append review_wake, and wake review_pending. Do NOT append a review_wake in the stalled branch (match node). Add a py/tests/test_tick.py case (test_review_stuck_escalation) asserting the escalation fires at the threshold.

tasks.title: Author the gate-parity proof
tasks.description: Spec-first: write docs/howto/gate-examples/gate-parity.sh — one DAG with gates covering pass (criteria true), fail (criteria false), the zero-criteria hollow floor (no criteria -> both runtimes must BLOCK), and a timeout (a criterion that sleeps past GATE_TIMEOUT_S with GATE_TIMEOUT_S=1 -> both BLOCK). Run each gate through BOTH runtimes (node bash .hb/gate.sh <G>; python hb gate <G> --dir) and assert identical pass/block outcomes per gate by comparing EXIT CODES (0=pass, non-0=block — the reliable cross-runtime signal, since the text output differs). Prints GATE-PARITY-OK only when every gate agrees across runtimes.

tasks.title: Author the doctor-parity proof
tasks.description: Spec-first: write docs/howto/gate-examples/doctor-parity.sh — a project with a COMPLETED phase whose gate criterion references a file that is then deleted (rot). Run doctor on BOTH runtimes (node node .hb/hb.js doctor; python hb doctor --dir) and assert both detect the rot — the rotted project's rot count must be > 0 on BOTH (not merely equal, so a both-zero bug can't pass vacuously) — and that a CLEAN project reports no rot on both. Prints DOCTOR-PARITY-OK only when the runtimes agree on rot detection. The tick keys off doctor's rot output, so a divergence here would wake the two runtimes differently.

tasks.description: Spec-first: write docs/howto/gate-examples/registry-parity.sh — derive the backend name set from BOTH runtimes (python: backends _KNOWN; node: the backend cases in plugin/templates/hb-exec.js defaultCmd). GATE_TICK.desc: Both runtimes' ticks emit the same data.reason (incl. review_stuck at the stall threshold); the Python review_stuck escalation is implemented; enforced by T82.

review.prompt: Refute that PTICK is done: does tick-parity.sh actually include a REVIEW-STALL fixture (review-owed gate with >= STUCK_TICKS review_wakes) that discriminates the runtimes, and did it go RED on the unfixed tick.py? Is the tick.py fix a real mirror of tick.sh (counts review_wakes since the last verdict; single-alert via a flag; no review_wake appended in the stalled branch), or a hack that only passes this fixture? Could TICK-PARITY-OK print if a fixture were skipped or both runtimes trivially agreed on an easy reason? Does the fix regress the normal review_pending path (a review that hasn't stalled still wakes review_pending)?
